hints.title: Use the same base
hints.body: Rewrite the square-root-of-two power with base 2. All three integrands can then be compared through their exponents.
hints.recap: Use the power-of-a-power rule to write expressions with a common base.
hints.pitfall: The three integrals have the same limits; you do not need their antiderivatives.

recall.reminder: Use the power-of-a-power rule to write expressions with a common base.

hints.title: Compare throughout the interval
hints.body: Between 0 and 1, compare x with half of x and with the square root of x. Use that ordering to compare powers with base 2.
hints.recap: A base greater than one preserves the order of exponents; power comparisons depend on the input interval.
hints.pitfall: Testing one input is not a proof for the whole interval.
hints.pause: Explain the ordering for every input strictly between the limits.

recall.reminder: A base greater than one preserves the order of exponents; power comparisons depend on the input interval.

hints.title: Compare the areas
hints.body: Draw the three positive curves in the order you found. The integral of each is its area over the same horizontal interval.
hints.recap: Strict ordering of continuous graph heights throughout a shared interval gives the same strict ordering of the integrals.
hints.pitfall: Equal heights at an endpoint do not make the whole areas equal.
hints.pause: Write the resulting strict order of P, Q and R.

recall.reminder: Strict ordering of continuous graph heights throughout a shared interval gives the same strict ordering of the integrals.

solution:
Rewrite the integrand of R: (2)x=(212)x=2x2.

For 0<x<1 we have x2<x<x. Since 2t increases as t increases, 2x2<2x<2x throughout the interior.

All three functions are continuous on [0, 1], and all three integrals have these same limits. Their strict interior ordering therefore gives R<Q<P: F. No explicit antiderivative is required.
